subject: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark
parts:
I have an app that makes use of the rgl and shinyRGL packages. It works with an installation of the open source shiny-server that I use for app development. However, it does not work properly specifically when moved to Spark.

On Spark, I can plot with rgl a number of data sets. However, for one dataset, the app crashes as soon as it finishes plotting. (The app grays out and reactivity is gone.) It is clear that rgl worked and one can still rotate the 3d image in the browser even though the app is no longer running. But this only happens on Spark. If I use my own hosted shiny-server, there are no crashes. It also plots much faster. This dataset is the largest of the four available to plot in the app. Could it be that there is some kind of resource limitation or time-out being hit on Spark? I wouldn't think the plot is that intensive, but maybe?

The app is here: http://spark.rstudio.com/uafsnap/plot3D/

On the "R plot3D examples" tab, select the "Hypsometry" dataset and the plot type "3D - interactive (rgl)". Everything else can be ignored. If you try this plot with the other data sets, the rgl plot works just fine. But with this one data set selected, the app will crash upon completion of the plot. I am unsure why this is only happening on Spark though. Can anyone suggest what the best methods would be that I could use to troubleshoot this problem? I cannot reproduce it in a simpler way or even as-is with this app on another server or localhost on a pc.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark
parts:
Hi Matthew,

That's an interesting problem; I haven't seen that before. We do have applications using shinyRGL running on Spark successfully: http://spark.rstudio.com/trestletech/bivar/

It may be that you're pushing the limits of WebGL further than those examples do, however. When you run this on the Open Source Shiny Server, is it running on the same network? I'm wondering if perhaps loading the RGL scene over a remote connection is such a big task that it's overwhelming the system.

Also, we disable web sockets on Spark. You can try replicating this on your server using this portion of the guide. Perhaps you'd be able to replicate the failure on your server without WebSockets?

Jeff

parts:
Hi Jeff,

I have tried the Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A option from the guide you reference but unfortunately nothing happens. It does not bring up any window to select or deselect protocols. This is the case if I go to the url for the app hosted on our own server with shiny-server, or if I launch the app with localhost from my Windows PC (maybe the latter is expected, not sure, but I figured it couldn't hurt to try). The window only comes up if I am using the app hosted on Spark, in which case all boxes are already checked by default, including websocket. Should websockets already be checked if it's disabled on Spark? Not sure why the window does not pop up on our own server. Perhaps it is something our IT person will have to disable.

Could you clarify what you mean by "When you run this on the Open Source Shiny Server, is it running on the same network?" and remote connection? Our server where we host apps with shiny-server for development is behind a firewall at our university so no one can access it unless on the university domain, either from on campus, or from a remote connection via VPN. But it turns out that even if I launch the app in the browser from home, it will work fine. But does this count as "remote" if I must use VPN to present my computer as though I am on the same domain/network as the server? I don't know if this addresses what you are asking though. Hopefully I have not butchered my Network vocabulary and I'm making some sense.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark
parts:
Hi Jeff,

We have two versions available on our server:

Shiny Server v1.0.0.42 / Node.js v0.10.21

and an older:

Shiny Server v0.3.3 / Node.js v0.10.0

I hadn't realized I was running on the old one when trying the Ctrl-Alt-Shift-A option. That does work with the newer version of course. The interesting thing is there are no rgl problems on either version of shiny-server. If I turn off websockets on the newer version it has serious effects, however. First, the "plot type" menu simply does not show up. However, if I move to the R Code tab which uses a different (conditional) sidebar, and then tab back, the "plot type" menu now appears. Soon after the app is liable to crash no matter what I do. Turning off websockets also cripples my use of shinyAce (initial load is fine but cannot update/make changes to font size or syntax highlighting theme). This all works fine on both the old and new shiny-server versions with websockets on.

Regarding Spark, whether I check websockets on or off in the popup window, the app often crashes in either case. However, it does not exhibit any issues with not fully building the UI right away or any issues with displaying R code with shinyAce.

Matt

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark
parts:
Yikes, alright. Well that seems to implicate our non-WebSocket protocols, then. If you can consistently get an app that works on WebSockets to fail by turning off WebSockets, that sounds pretty damning. Spark currently has WebSockets disabled on the server-side, so you checking or unchecking it from the client shouldn't make a difference, so the behavior that you see (consistent unreliability on Spark) sounds right if the app doesn't work without WebSockets.

Is your application open-source? I'd be interested in trying to host it on another server or accessing it from another client. One more thing: do you consistently see the same behavior when accessing the application on Spark from another network (your home, coffee shop, whatever)? I ask because the quirkiest network problems we've encountered have consistently been on University networks. We've seen issues with users on a college campus not be able to access an internal Shiny Server because the University blocks certain ports, or filters traffic of certain types, etc.

If the app is open source, I can try setting it up on a server that has WebSockets enabled to see if you can get it to work from your campus. That would definitely confirm that this is a WebSockets issue.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: App using rgl works with shiny-server but crashes on Spark
parts:
Hi,

It tentatively appears I may have fixed the problem (though not solved it). I minimized the degree to which my usage of RGL was representing an edge case scenario, bringing it more in line with simpler applications. The code on github previously linked to has been changed. At least so far, I can now use RGL to plot my various datasets of various size in the app hosted on Spark without websockets and I have not yet seen any crashes (which tended to be fairly quick and easy to produce before).

The key difference from before is now I have no reactive inputs defined on the server side and sent to the UI side via uiOutput. Now they are build directly on the UI side. Specifically, I used to have a menu for selecting the type of plot to make (e.g. 2d or 3d, static or rgl, etc.), where the choices were conditional upon the dataset chosen in a prior menu since not all plots were appropriate for all datasets, requiring the reactive element to be defined on the server side. Although the conditional menu was ideal, and I use this approach often in many other apps/contexts, I did away with it here. The app loses soem elegance as a result. For example now someone can click a plot tab for a plot that is not available for a given dataset, and they will see a message saying so instead of seeing a plot. I'd rather they not have the 'bait and switch' experience. But at least now the app seems to be working with the edge case removed.

I don't know for certain this was the problem. But in general I have noticed that I encounter far more bugs and app-breaking events the more extreme I get with complex dynamic server-side reactive elements. I've had much mroe complex dynamic UI than in this case, but it seems the combination of the way I was going about it, along with RGL and how they interacted, was causing problems.

Matt

Is your application open-source? I'd be interested in trying to host it on another server or accessing it from another client. Jeff
